title: Activation cadence and signal synchronization — scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for cross-functional activation cadence (timing) and how we synchronize signals across product, SRE, serving-runtime, and solutions-eng when we do micro-releases / canaries / A/B slices for LLM features.

Context / problem statement:
- We frequently run short-lived canaries that exercise new routing, model variants, or safety filters. Observability is fragmented across teams (console metrics, infra traces, eval harness). We need an explicit cadence and a single-source checklist for the first 48 hours so teams can move quickly and avoid noisy rollbacks.
- Goal: reduce rollbacks due to missed signal, speed up safe ramp from 0.1% to 10%, and make human gating predictable.

Key definitions (as we'll use them here):
- Micro-release: a staged activation of a behavior/model variant targeting <=5% traffic initially.
- Activation cadence: the timing plan (how long at each exposure step and when to escalate).
- Safety signal: automated metric(s) that will block or pause ramp (latency P95, error rate, hallucination-rate proxy).
- Human gate: a named, paged individual or small group who must sign-off to proceed beyond a cadence step.

Quick checklist (first 48h canonical):
- Pre-launch (T-minus 72h):
  - Confirm rollout config in Console and that canary slice is instrumented. (owner: product engineer)
  - Link PR + rollout plan in meeting notes and add to experiment contract. (owner: PM)
  - Smoke tests on staging (end-to-end with KV-cache warm). (owner: eng/serving-runtime)
  - Alert subscriptions: oncall, product-owner, model-owner, SRE-champion. Slack channel: #rollouts-activation. (owner: SRE)
  - Baseline snapshots: capture 48h baseline for key signals (latency distribution, token-cost-per-request, model-confusion/eval signal). (owner: observability)
additional_notes:
Activation cadence proposal (template):
- Step 0: dark-launch validation (0% traffic) — run synthetic load, smoke for 6h
- Step 1: 0.05% for 30m — quick health check and basic metric sweep
- Step 2: 0.5% for 2h — monitor anomaly detectors and qualitative review of ~200 responses
- Step 3: 2% for 6h — extended telemetry + hold for human gate signoff
- Step 4: 5-10% for 12h — monitor cost/latency economics and user-facing metrics
- Step 5: roll to 100% or schedule next increment depending on experiment

Signals to synchronize across teams (important to agree on a single canonical source and thresholds):
- Infra: P50/P95 latency, GPU utilization, request queue length, retries per request
- Model/Quality: failure-rate (server error), hallucination-proxy (rerank delta / anchor score drop), token-overage rate, top-k repetition spikes
- Product/Business: engaged sessions affected, opt-outs, conversion delta (for features that map to revenue)
- Cost: tokens per response, average inference cost per call

Suggested blocking thresholds (starting proposal — conservative):
- P95 latency increase > 40% vs baseline for 30m -> PAUSE and page SRE
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% absolute or 3x baseline -> PAUSE and page serving-runtime
- Hallucination proxy increase > 2x baseline on a sliding 1h window -> PAUSE and page model-owner
- Token cost per call > 30% increase -> REVIEW with cost steward (can be non-blocking depending on business)

Human gates and contact matrix (example):
- Gate A (after Step 2): product + model-owner must ACK in Slack thread and file short comment in rollout log (who: PM + model lead)
- Gate B (after Step 3): SRE + runtime lead + product must jointly OK to proceed. If anyone disagrees, hold for deeper triage and revert to previous config

Comms templates (Slack snippets):
- Pre-launch: "Rolling out [experiment-name] to X slice. Baseline captured. Alerts: @oncall @sre-champ @pm. Will open thread for signals. Estimated timeline: 48h."
- Pause template: "PAUSING rollout [experiment-name] at Step {n}. Signal: {metric} breached ({value}). Paging: @serving-runtime @sre @model-owner. Time: {hh:mm}. Rolling back traffic to previous variant."

Telemetry quick-queries (examples to copy into console):
- latency P95: SELECT quantile(0.95, latency_ms) FROM requests WHERE variant='experiment-123' GROUP BY 1m
- hallucination proxy: compute rerank delta for QA prompts in eval-set: (see linked eval harness CONFLUENCE-INVOC-2047)
- token cost: SUM(tokens_out + tokens_in) / COUNT(request_id) FILTER BY variant

Rollback decision tree (simplified):
- If blocking threshold hit and automated rollback configured -> immediate rollback -> open incident -> notify stakeholders
- If threshold hit but noisy (single spike) -> pause ramp, increase sample size, manual check of qualitative examples for 30-60m
- If multiple blocking signals (latency + hallucination) -> immediate rollback and incident bridge

Post-activation notes (what to capture in the rollout log):
- timestamped decisions + reason
- exact config ids (model sha, quantization profile, routing policy)
- link to sampling set of model outputs used for qualitative review
- cost delta over baseline (first 24h and 72h)

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Do we want a single global playbook for all LLM canaries or separate for rerankers vs generator models? Differences in signals (e.g., hallucination proxies) may warrant separate templates. (action: product + research to propose)
- Where is the canonical place for the short qualitative sample? Right now samples live in Confluence and in a dataset S3; should standardize to Console-linked artifact. (action: obs eng + docs)
- Should we auto-suppress non-critical alerts during first 10min of each step to avoid signal noise? Risk: miss real issues. (action: SRE to prototype suppression window for next test)

Notes from last micro-release (experiment-247):
- Missed step: we didn't warm KV cache in staging -> initial Step 1 P95 spike, delayed Step 2 by 90m
- What worked: pre-captured qualitative sample made it easy to see a subtle distributional issue in template prompts
- Action items taken: add staging KV warm step to pre-launch checklist; add a metric for cold-cache request fraction

Quick wins / proposals to trial next sprint:
- Single rollout dashboard widget that shows the 6 canonical signals side-by-side and highlights which team owns each metric
- Lightweight sign-off UI in Console where gate owners can tick to proceed and write one-line rationale (auto-appends to rollout log)
- Experiment labels that make it easy to scope alerts to only relevant slices (avoid paging on global alarms)

If you're reading this and want to help: add comments inline, paste relevant queries, and tag what you can own for the TODOs above. This is intentionally a working doc — keep it lean and iterative.

-- Asha
